folder_html:
LIVE PRECIPITATION

Precipitation intensity (MRMS quality-controlled composite reflectivity, dBZ, OBSERVED radar echo): LOWEST 5 Very Light cyan/blue (drizzle, mist) → Light greens (~20-30: light rain/snow) → Moderate dark green (~30-40: steady rain/snow) → Heavy yellow/orange (~40-50: heavy rain) → Severe red (~50-60: severe storms, hail possible) → Intense magenta/purple (~60-70: violent storms, large hail) → HIGHEST+ 70+ Extreme white (destructive hail, debris). Same dBZ always shows the same color in every season — rain, snow, lake-effect snow, thunderstorms. The quality-controlled mosaic filters non-precipitation echoes (ground clutter, migrating birds/insects), so clear air stays see-through and only real precipitation paints.

How to read it in any season. Light greens are light rain in summer — and light snow in winter. Moderate dark green is steady rain or steady snow, including lake-effect bands. Heavy yellow/orange is heavy rain (or very heavy snow rates). Severe red means severe thunderstorms with hail possible; Intense magenta/purple means violent storms with large hail and flash flooding; Extreme white is reserved for the most destructive echoes. Radar sees precipitation particles, not air temperature, so one scale covers rain, snow, and thunderstorms all year. Where you see through the overlay, there is no precipitation right now.
